It combines intelligent understanding of creative intent with the ability to build visual worlds: with precise instruction following, it develops a creative concept into concrete characters, scenes and atmosphere. Generation and editing are unified in one checkpoint, which generates images from text (text-to-image) and edits one or more reference images (image editing), giving creators and developers a flexible and controllable way to create images. It generates images of about 16 megapixels at every aspect ratio, from 4096x4096 (1:1) to 6272x2688 (21:9), directly and without an upscaler (see [Sizes](#sizes)). The checkpoint is distilled to 6 sampling steps (6 NFEs) with no classifier-free guidance. Its diffusion transformer (DiT) has the H3 architecture without the audio layers, and it uses the MiniMax-H3 text encoder unchanged. ![Fifteen MiniMax-H3-Image text-to-image results in landscape and portrait formats: a 3D fantasy battle, a blue-green landscape painting, a tree frog, an indigo-dyed rabbit, a 3D white-haired girl, a portrait among flowers, a sci-fi city, dumplings, a highland cow, a mirror portrait, a 3D otter and sheep, a pixel art cat, a jewel beetle, giant cherries and a fisheye selfie](assets/showcase_hero.jpg) **Highlights** MiniMax-H3-Image brings together three core strengths: speed, image quality, and instruction following. 1. **16-megapixel images at a practical computational cost.** Compared with the 1–4 MP outputs common today, 16 MP (4096 × 4096) images offer far more detail but typically require substantially more computation. MiniMax-H3-Image keeps that computational cost manageable, making 16 MP generation practical for everyday creation. 2. **Rich detail. Remarkable realism.** MiniMax-H3-Image goes beyond the familiar “AI look” to produce images with intricate detail and lifelike realism, opening up more possibilities for creative and professional use. It brings generated imagery closer to the richness and nuance of the real visual world. 3. **Stronger instruction following.** Greater creative control. Great image generation goes beyond beautiful pictures—it helps creators bring their ideas to life. MiniMax-H3-Image delivers the strongest instruction following among open-source models and supports up to 16 reference images, giving creators more control over the final result. ## Model Zoo | Model | Role | Precision | Size | Hugging Face | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **MiniMax-H3-Image** | Text-to-image and image editing | BF16 (DiT) | 68.65 GB | [MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxA

# Arete-27B

We post-trained over Alibaba's Qwen3.8-27B to reinforce western values on a Chinese-trained model. We call this new model Arete-27B.

Open source models give labs the raw tools to mold intelligence to varied preferences. The values a model ships with should not be the only values its users get to choose from. We observed firsthand refusals, deflections, and CCP-framed answers on politically sensitive topics in Qwen3.8-27B, and post-trained to alter those biases.

On our evaluation, Arete-27B raised its fact score from 2.32 to 2.98 out of 5 and cut answers containing propaganda from 22% to 0.9%. The improvement held in all seven value categories, without a meaningful regression on the general-capability and agentic benchmarks we ran.

That is not to claim that we remedied all behaviors associated with the extant viewpoint, but that we have addressed a potential root cause. We believe it's important that labs and researchers continue to create models that align with their values and worldviews, and we are thankful that companies like Alibaba provide the raw materials to do so.

[Blog post](https://nousresearch.com/arete) · [Evaluation](https://huggingface.co/datasets/NousResearch/Propaganda_Eval)

## Model details

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Developer | Nous Research |
| Model | Arete-27B |
| Starting model | Alibaba's Qwen3.8-27B |
| Parameter scale | 27B |
| Post-training | Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) |
| Evaluated checkpoint | Step 1,202 |
| Teacher | Inkling |
| Post-training data | Text-only |
| Training context | 64k |

We used supervised fine-tuning only. No RL, no preference optimization, and no architectural modification.

## What we trained for

We focused on seven value categories:

- Freedom of expression
- State ideology
- State versus free market
- Education
- Data privacy and surveillance
- Democracy
- Environmental Policy

Before we could begin post-training we had to measure what we were shooting for. We separated factual recall, the ability to corroborate verified sources of truth, from framing: whether an answer adopts the Chinese state's account as its own.

Arete-27B is intended for general assistance and agentic work where users want this change in viewpoint, and for research into how post-training changes a model's values and behavior. We encourage the community to test it against their own requirements and continue experimenting with value-alignment.

## Teacher and dataset

We needed to choose a model whose answers on these topics we were willing to teach from. We used a combination of benchmarks, including our own evaluation, and researcher judgement to assess the more intangible qualitative output we were hoping to impart. We chose Inkling as the best open model with a positive eval on what we were targeting. Using an open teacher also avoided the terms-of-use restrictions associated with "illicit distillation."

We generated twenty thousand prompts across the seven categories through a deduplication-enforced pipeline, checked them against the held-out evaluation set and removed the overlap we found, and collected teacher responses alongside the starting model's own. Every batch of data moved through reviewed pull requests, the same way we ship code.

The blog post announces publication of the training dataset. See the blog post for release links; the linked `Propaganda_Eval` dataset is the held-out evaluation, not the training dataset.

## Training

We fine-tuned Qwen3.8-27B on about 52.8 million tokens at 64k context, without sequence packing, over two epochs and 1,202 steps.

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Optimizer | AdamW |
| Adam betas | (0.9, 0.98) |
| Epsilon | 1e-5 |
| Weight decay | 0.1 |
| Gradient clipping | 1.0 |
| Learning rate | Linear warmup from 1e-6 to 1e-5 over the first 120 steps, then cosine decay to 1e-6 at step 1,202 |
| Batch size | 48 |
| Epochs | 2, shuffled each epoch |
| Steps | 1,202 total; 601 per epoch |
| Precision | bf16 compute with fp32 master weights and optimizer states |
| Parallelism | Tensor parallel 4 |
| Trained weights | All language-model weights |
| Frozen weights | Vision encoder; our data is text-only |
| Disabled during training | Multi-token-prediction (MTP) head |
| Sequence packing | None |

Training loss fell quickly during the 120-step warmup and leveled off near 1.0 by the end of epoch 1. It stepped down to about 0.8 when epoch 2 began, because the model was seeing the same examples a second time, and stayed flat from there. Gradient norm started near 32 and settled around 1.4 once warmup ended.

## Measuring the problem

Our [propaganda evaluation](https://huggingface.co/datasets/NousResearch/Propaganda_Eval) contains 803 prompts spanning the seven value categories above. Prompts come from English-language government statutes, news and research reports, with no single source supplying more than 13 prompts.

For each prompt we extracted 2–4 required facts from a dated source article, along with the official-frame language the CCP uses on that topic. An LLM judge, Grok 4.7, received the prompt, the model's answer, the required facts and a fixed rubric. The judge was not told which model wrote the answer.

We developed the judge on a 25-prompt pilot that we graded by hand, revising the rubric three times wherever the judge and the human grades disagreed. The main fix was defining a stated fact by its substance rather than its exact wording, dates or citations. Before training, we removed every training prompt that overlapped the evaluation set.

### Factual recall

The judge marks each required fact as stated, missed or opposed. A fact is opposed when the answer denies it or gives the state's account instead. We compute a score for each prompt using the following rubric:

| Score | Meaning |

Qwen3.8-27B brings these advances to a compact, deployment-friendly dense model: a native vision-language model that understands images and videos, with flexible thinking control, designed to carry complex, multi-step tasks through to completion with greater reliability. ## Qwen3.8 Highlights Qwen3.8-27B features the following enhancements: - **Core Capabilities**: Comprehensive improvements across coding, professional work, research, and long-horizon agentic tasks. - **Agent Execution**: Stronger autonomous planning and better handling of environment feedback, leading to more reliable end-to-end task completion. - **Downstream Compatibility**: Broader support for popular harnesses and development tools, making it easier to integrate into your existing stack. - **Flexible Thinking Control**: Thinking mode is on by default and can be disabled per request; reasoning depth can be tuned with `reasoning_effort`, and reasoning context from historical messages is retained via `preserve_thinking`. - **Vision-Language Understanding**: Native support for image and video understanding, from STEM diagrams and documents to hour-scale videos. ## Model Overview - Type: Causal Language Model with Vision Encoder - Training Stage: Pre-training & Post-training - Language Model - Number of Parameters: 27B - Hidden Dimension: 5120 - Token Embedding: 248,320 (Padded) - Number of Layers: 64 - Hidden Layout: 16 × (3 × (Gated DeltaNet → FFN) → 1 × (Gated Attention → FFN)) - Gated DeltaNet: - Number of Linear Attention Heads: 48 for V and 16 for QK - Head Dimension: 128 - Gated Attention: - Number of Attention Heads: 24 for Q and 4 for KV - Head Dimension: 256 - Rotary Position Embedding Dimension: 64 - Feed Forward Network: - Intermediate Dimension: 17,408 - LM Output: 248,320 (Padded) - MTP (Multi-Token Prediction): trained with multiple steps - Context Length: 262,144 natively and extensible up to 1,000,000 tokens. ## Benchmark Results ### Text Performance

--- license: apache-2.0 library_name: idol pipeline_tag: image-to-3d tags: - gaussian-splatting - 3d - image-to-3d ---

Idol

A single image to a 3D Gaussian splat.
One picture of an object in, up to a million 3D Gaussians out, including the sides the picture never showed.

Idol turns one picture of an object into a 3D Gaussian splat. Give it a render, a generated image or a photo: it removes the background, frames the object and generates up to 1,048,576 Gaussians, written as a standard 3DGS `.ply`. It runs on consumer GPUs, using 7.2 GB of VRAM and can run in under 2 seconds.
## Examples Idol turns one picture of an object into a 3D Gaussian splat. Give it a render, a generated image or a photo: it removes the background, frames the object and generates up to 1,048,576 Gaussians, including the sides the picture never showed. It runs on consumer GPUs, using 7.2 GB of VRAM and can run in under 2 seconds.
## Get started **1. Get access to the image encoders.** Idol reads its input through two gated models on Hugging Face. Accept their terms with your Hugging Face account, then log in once with `hf auth login` (or set `HF_TOKEN`): - [facebook/dinov3-vith16plus-pretrain-lvd1689m](https://huggingface.co/facebook/dinov3-vith16plus-pretrain-lvd1689m) - [black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-dev](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-dev) (only its VAE is downloaded) **2. Install the code** ```bash git clone https://github.com/speridlabs/idol-sdk.git cd idol-sdk pip install -e . # Python 3.10+, PyTorch 2.5+, an NVIDIA GPU with CUDA ``` There is no separate download step: on the first run, Idol's weights (about 3 GB, from this repository) and the two image encoders download automatically into the Hugging Face cache. If the encoders are not accessible yet, Idol stops before downloading anything and says what is missing. **3. Generate a 3D object** ```bash python -m idol.sample --image photo.jpg --mode real python -m idol.sample --image renders/ --mode synthetic --out outputs ``` For each image this writes `.ply` (open it in any Gaussian splat viewer), `_input.png` (the image the model saw, after background removal and cropping) and `_camera.json` (the predicted camera of the input). Pick the mode for your input. It sets how much room the crop leaves around the object: | `--mode` | for | crop | |---|---|---| | `synthetic` (default) | renders and generated images of a single object | object fills 1/1.2 of the frame | | `real` | photographs | object fills 1/1.7 of the frame | From Python: ```python from idol import IdolPipeline pipeline = IdolPipeline.from_pretrained("speridlabs/idol") output = pipeline("photo.jpg", mode="real", seed=42, num_gaussians=1_048_576) output.gaussian.save_ply("photo.ply") ``` ## Flags | Flag | Default | What it does | |---|---|---| | `--seed` | 42 | Fix it to get the same object again. | | `--steps` | 50 | Sampling steps. Fewer are faster but lose some detail. | | `--cfg_strength` | 3.0 | Classifier-free guidance: how strictly the object follows the image. | | `--rescale_t` | 3.0 | Time shift: higher spends more steps on the overall shape, lower on fine detail. | | `--num_gaussians` | 262144 | 32,768 to 1,048,576, a multiple of 32. | | `--dinov3_dtype` | bf16 | `fp32` runs the DINOv3 encoder in full precision (1.7 GB more memory). | | `--weights` | `speridlabs/idol` | A Hugging Face repo or a local folder. | | `--no_optimize` | optimized | Turn off the faster sampling. | Faster sampling is on by default on GPU (~1.7x, same output quality): the denoiser is compiled with `torch.compile`, the guided and unguided passes run as one batch, and attention uses cuDNN with TF32 matmuls while sampling. The first image in a process is slower while it compiles. ## More details about the model | Component | Parameters | Precision on GPU | Weights in VRAM | |---|---|---|---| | DiT (denoiser) | 370.6M | FP16 transformer blocks; FP32 embeddings and norms | ~0.8–1.0 GB | | Octree decoder | 50.8M | FP16 transformer blocks; FP32 embeddings and norms | ~0.1–0.2 GB | | Gaussian decoder | 237.3M | FP16 transformer blocks; FP32 embeddings and norms | ~0.5–0.9 GB | | BiRefNet (background removal) | 220.7M | FP16 | ~0.44 GB | | DINOv3 ViT-H+/16 | 840.6M | bf16 | ~1.68 GB | | FLUX.2 VAE | 84.1M | bf16 (FP32 checkpoint, cast on load) | ~0.17 GB | | **Full request** | **~1.80B** | mostly FP16 / bf16, some FP32 | **~3.7–4.4 GB of weights, 7.2 GB peak** | ## Benchmark Idol, TripoSplat, TRELLIS and LGM, scored at the input view (PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, IoU) and at seven new views (DINOv2, CLIP, sharpness distance). Mean scores, 1 × H100 per model. Bold is the best in each column. | Model | Setting |

## 1. Model Introduction Kimi K3.1 Pro is an open-weight, natively multimodal agentic model, and our most capable 3T-class model to date. Post-trained from Kimi K3 with large-scale joint reinforcement learning across hundreds of downstream domains, it is the first model in the K3.1 series. With a 1-million-token context window, Kimi K3.1 Pro delivers substantial improvements in coding, 3D creation, financial research, factual accuracy, and other agentic capabilities. ## 2. --- license: apache-2.0 pipeline_tag: text-to-speech library_name: zonos3 language: - en - fr - es - de - it - pt - nl - pl - ru - sv - tr - uk - cs - da - fi - el - hu - "no" - ro - sk - bg - zh - ja - ko - ar - he - vi - id - th - tl - ms - ka - hi - bn - ta - te - mr - gu - kn - ml - pa - or - ur tags: - text-to-speech - tts - speech-synthesis - voice-cloning - multilingual - gguf - zonos - zonos3 - zyphra --- # ZONOS3-Mini

--- ZONOS3-Mini is Zyphra’s compact, open-source text-to-speech model, delivering natural reliable speech and high-fidelity voice cloning with just 100 million active parameters. It runs in real time on phones and laptops, including directly in the browser. Clone a voice from an audio sample, or design a character by shaping age, accent and vocal texture. Steer emotion, pace and delivery down to individual words for games, narration and voice assistants. Run ZONOS3-Mini locally with our browser and native runtimes, or access it through [Zyphra Cloud](https://cloud.zyphra.com/models/zyphra/ZONOS3-Mini). Model weights are released under Apache 2.0. **Model details, samples and evaluations are in the [blog post](https://www.zyphra.com/our-work/zonos3-mini).** **A hosted version is available at [Zyphra Cloud](https://cloud.zyphra.com/models/zyphra/ZONOS3-Mini).** ## Languages ZONOS3-Mini supports 43 languages. | Region | Languages | |---|---| | Western and Southern Europe | English, French, Spanish, German, Italian, Portuguese, Dutch, Greek | | Northern Europe | Swedish, Danish, Norwegian, Finnish | | Central and Eastern Europe | Polish, Czech, Slovak, Hungarian, Romanian, Bulgarian, Russian, Ukrainian | | Middle East and Caucasus | Turkish, Arabic, Hebrew, Georgian | | East Asia | Mandarin Chinese, Japanese, Korean | | Southeast Asia | Vietnamese, Indonesian, Malay, Thai, Tagalog | | South Asia | Hindi, Bengali, Tamil, Telugu, Marathi, Gujarati, Kannada, Malayalam, Punjabi, Odia, Urdu | ## Quick start ### In your browser ZONOS3-Mini runs entirely on your own GPU through WebGPU: no install and no server. The first visit downloads the model, and the browser keeps it cached for later visits. You need a browser with WebGPU support. - [Zonos Voice Studio](https://zyphra.com/zonos3-mini/localplayground#cast): the full studio. - [Lite](https://zyphra.com/zonos3-mini/localplayground/lite): quick voice cloning. Pick, upload or record a voice and speak with it. ### With SGLang [SGLang-Omni](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni) serves ZONOS3-Mini on NVIDIA GPUs behind the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/audio/speech` endpoint, with streaming and voice cloning from a reference clip (no transcript needed). Install SGLang-Omni by following its [installation guide](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/blob/main/docs/get_started/installation.md), then start a server: ```bash sgl-omni serve --model-path Zyphra/ZONOS3-Mini --port 8000 ``` Once `curl http://localhost:8000/health` reports `"healthy"`, generate speech with the default voice from another terminal: ```bash curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/v1/audio/speech \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"input": "Hello from ZONOS3-Mini!"}' \ --output output.wav ``` Add `"references": [{"audio_path": ""}]` to clone a voice, or `"stream": true, "response_format": "pcm"` to stream 44.1 kHz audio as it is generated. The [ZONOS3 cookbook](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/blob/main/docs/cookbook/zonos3.md) covers voice cloning, streaming and the sampling options. ### Native runtimes The [ZONOS3-Mini GitHub repository](https://github.com/Zyphra/ZONOS3-Mini) holds Zyphra's own runtimes, which share one HTTP API and serve the Zonos Voice Studio: a CUDA server for NVIDIA GPUs, an MLX server for Apple Silicon, a C++/ggml server and CLI (CPU, CUDA, Metal or Vulkan), and the in-browser WebGPU build. They load the GGUF files in [`gguf/`](https://huggingface.co/Zyphra/ZONOS3-Mini/tree/main/gguf) and the WebGPU shards in [`web/`](https://huggingface.co/Zyphra/ZONOS3-Mini/tree/main/web); the 27 default voices, grouped by language, are in [`gguf/voices/`](https://huggingface.co/Zyphra/ZONOS3-Mini/blob/main/gguf/voices/README.md). ## Architecture (rough outline) Text is NeMo-normalized (English, Mandarin, Japanese, Korean, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Portuguese; other languages pass through as written) and encoded with an 8,192-entry SuperBPE tokenizer. The language model autoregressively generates 15 Hz dual-codec frames (10 codebooks of 4,096 entries each: one semantic codebook distilled from the Wav2Vec2-BERT teacher plus nine acoustic codebooks), conditioned on the text, a speaker prompt and three bucketed acoustic controls. A causal multi-resolution iSTFT head renders the frames to 44.1 kHz audio as they are produced. ![ZONOS3-Mini inference pipeline](assets/zonos3_mini_arloop_animated.gif) *Inference pipeline.
